To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) class 1 integromediated antibiotic resistance genes are widespread in soils and related habitats, (2) IncP-1plasmids carrying class1 integrons are enriched in the rhizo sphere, and (3) the class 1 gene cassettes qacEΔ1 and sul1 are the predominant integron gene cassettes in the soils and related ecosystems analyzed.
the class 1 intI1 gene and qacE and/or qacEΔ1 resistance genes are present in all investigated environmental samples, and that the qacEΔΔ1 genes are present on IncP-1 type plasmids.
the class 1 integration gene intI1 is widely spread in soils with or without human input.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the first cultivation-independent analysis of class 1 integrases, qacE and related genes in a variety of environmental samples, and it provides evidence for the presence and enrichment of IncP-1-related class 1 integons in soils and related environments.

the first comprehensive cultivation-independent analysis of the occurrence of genes associated with class 1 integros in soils and related environments and the first evidence of the association of class 1 integrins with IncP- 1 plasmids in the rhizopshere.

the first cultivation-independent detection and quantification of the class 3 integron components intI1, sul1, and qacE and their correlation to the IncP-1 ε plasmid-specific korB gene in soils and rhizospheres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the class 1 gene cassettes are widespread and abundant in soils and related environments, and their dissemination might be facilitated by IncP-1-like plasmids.

class 1 integons and genes typically associated with them are widespread disseminated in the environment, but their association with plasmids and their transfer and spread in the environment is still unclear.
class 1 integons and IncP-1 are widespread in soils and related habitats, which is a matter of great concern, especially in view of the increasing application of manure as a fertilizer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
class 1 integon components are widespread in agricultural and related environments and are often related to IncP-1plasmids.
class 1 integons are widespread in the environments analyzed and their dissemination is facilitated by IncP-1-type plasmids.
class 1 integons are widespread in soils and related habitats and that IncP- 1 plasmids contribute to their dissemination.
The main takeaway from our work is that

IncP- 1 plasmids carrying integron gene cassettes are abundant in the environments analyzed and that rhizosphere of crops might be hot spots for the exchange and dissemination of antibiotic resistance determinants.
the dissemination of class 11 integrons and associated resistance genes is not restricted to the clinical setting but is also a common feature of agricultural environments.

class 1 integons, and in particular qacEΔ1 genes, are abundant in the environments analyzed and that IncP- 1 plasmids carrying these genes may be important for the spread of class-1 integrons in these environments.
